turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in, sit. You look worn out. What brings you?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): The wheezing, it is not stopping. And I have been waiting so long, I am really tired.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am sorry about the wait. Start from when you first felt unwell.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): First it was cold and cough. Then the chest became tight and this whistling started. I am having wheezing since then only.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did the cold begin?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, ten days back... no, actually two weeks. Week before last, I remember Monday. So two weeks.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the wheezing itself?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Four days... wait, let me think. Sunday night, so that is three days. Three days of this whistle.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is it constant, or does it come and go?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): More in the night. I am not able to sleep. Lying down it gets worse. If I walk to the bus stop I have to stop and stand.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any pain in the chest with it?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No, not pain. Tightness, like someone tied a band. But not pain.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): When you cough, any blood?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that. Cough is there, mostly dry. Sometimes a little white phlegm, that is all.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): And I had to take leave from office. My manager was not at all happy. What to do, I cannot sit there whistling.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): We will come to the office in a minute. Was there any fever?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): In the beginning, for two days, mild fever was there. That has gone. Now no fever.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about the nose and the throat?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Sore throat has settled. Nose is still a little blocked, more in the morning.
[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): This tiredness, is it new with this illness?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, from the cold itself I am tired. Today I am more short with people, sorry. I didn't sleep.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): No need to apologise. Have you had asthma before, or is this new?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Asthma is there from when I was twelve. My father also has it. I keep inhalers at home.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Tell me which inhalers, and how you have been using them.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Blue one and brown one. When the chest is tight I grab the brown... or the blue? I always mix those two up. It is annoying.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): We will sort it out slowly. What names are written on them?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Blue is Asthalin, that is salbutamol. Brown is Beclate. The brown is hundred microgram... no, two hundred. I saw the label last night. Two hundred.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): For the Asthalin, how many puffs, and how often these last few days?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Two puffs each time. Maybe five, six times a day. I don't count properly, whenever the whistle comes I take it.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the Beclate, what were you told?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Two puffs in the morning and two at night. But I take it only when I remember. Some days I skip the whole thing. I thought the blue one was the daily one.

[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back. Blue Asthalin, the reliever, two puffs when you are tight, and you have needed it maybe five or six times a day. Brown Beclate two hundred, the preventer, meant to be two puffs twice a day, but you miss doses. Is that correct?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that is correct. Blue helps a little, maybe one hour, then the whistle is back. Brown I don't feel any effect so I leave it.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Very common mix-up, you are not the first. Any other tablets or syrups?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only these two inhalers. Nothing else.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergy to a medicine, or to anything else?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing that I know of.
[SEG0038] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Never. I don't like the smell itself.

[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Before I listen, the nurse read your peak flow. She has written three hundred and twenty... one second, I am looking at the wrong column. Best of three is three hundred and ten litres. Three ten.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that very bad? I don't even know my normal number. Nobody told me.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): It is on the low side for your age. On her chart the oxygen is ninety-seven percent, pulse is ninety-six, temperature thirty-six point eight. Let me listen to the chest.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. I just want something so I can sleep tonight, that is all. Can we not drag this.

[SEG0044] person_1 (DOCTOR): There is a wheeze on both sides, louder when you breathe out. I am not hearing any crackles. You are managing full sentences, which is reassuring. No swelling around the ankles.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): So the cold has gone into the chest, is it? Just tell me straight.

[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working impression is a flare of your asthma after that viral cold. I cannot fully rule out a chest infection, but with no fever now and the phlegm not looking dirty, infection is less likely.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Please don't send me for a pile of tests. I have a meeting tomorrow, I should not even be sitting here.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not booking an x-ray today. If the breathing has not eased after the steroid course, we might do a chest x-ray then.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Steroid? You mean tablets?
[SEG0050] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yes. I will start prednisolone, thirty milligrams... no, forty milligrams, once every morning for five days, by mouth, with food. That is for this flare.
[SEG0051] person_2 (PATIENT): Five days and then I stop, or I have to continue?

[SEG0052] person_1 (DOCTOR): Five days and then stop. No taper for this short course. Keep the blue Asthalin, two puffs when the wheeze comes, ideally with a spacer. If you are needing it more than six times in a day, that is too much, come back sooner.
[SEG0053] person_2 (PATIENT): Spacer is there somewhere in the cupboard. I will look tonight. If I find it.

[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Please use it. And the brown Beclate, two puffs morning and two at night, every single day, even on days you feel fine. You will not feel it working straight away, that is why it gets left.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): Alright, I will try. I am just so fed up of this whistle sound.

[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): One safety thing. If you cannot finish a sentence for breathlessness, or the blue inhaler stops helping, or the lips look bluish, go to emergency the same day. Don't wait for the appointment.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay, okay, I heard you. When is the appointment then?
[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come back and see me in one week, whether you are better or not, and we will repeat the peak flow. Anything you want to ask?
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Just write the tablet and let me go home and sleep. Thank you.

spec.situation: Teenager or adult wheezy after a cold; confuses blue and brown inhaler; uses the reliever 'maybe five, six times a day'; peak flow numbers read by the nurse. Doctor adds a steroid course.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.

bad.reason: Two-week cold supported, but current cold status not clearly stated; only blocked nose persists.

omissions.text: Shortness of breath on exertion: when walking to the bus stop the patient has to stop and stand.
Current shortness of breath worsens when lying down and is preventing sleep.
Patient reports blue Asthalin helps only a little, for about one hour, then wheezing returns.
Beclate adherence is not just uncertain; patient says some days they skip the whole inhaler and previously thought the blue inhaler was the daily one.
Prednisolone was specifically advised to be taken with food.
Doctor advised using Asthalin ideally with a spacer, and patient said they have a spacer at home somewhere and will look for it tonight.
Doctor said no chest x-ray is being booked today.
